items.title: Fine particles from aircraft exhaust become more harmful over time, lab tests suggest
items.summary: Fine particulate matter consists of tiny particles with diameters in the nanometer range. They are produced, for example, by fuel combustion, remain suspended in the air and can penetrate deep into the respiratory tract. There, they can trigger oxidative stress, a process that promotes inflammation and, over the long term, can lead to serious health problems such as respiratory or cardiovascular diseases. Scientists call this harmful property the particles' oxidative potential.

Operated by the Army and Royal Air Force with the aim of detecting low flying aircraft at 500 feet (150 m), early warning could then be sent to Swansea upon discovering incoming German bombers. The entire structure was decommissioned in 1945 at the war's conclusion. items.summary: arXiv:2610.17950v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Traditional optical system design for imaging applications has long been guided by image quality metrics such as geometrical RMS spot size, wavefront error, and modulation transfer function (MTF). items.summary: arXiv:2610.14136v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Iterative sampling in diffusion models can lead to error accumulation due to exposure bias. items.title: Long-Horizon-Terminal-Bench 2.0: Automating Diverse Task Construction and Measuring Sustained Agent Progress
items.summary: arXiv:2610.14146v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-horizon terminal benchmarks measure whether an agent can sustain progress through extended workflows with process rewards, not only whether its final state passes a binary check. We present Long-Horizon-Terminal-Bench 2.0 (LHTB 2.0), an extension of Long-Horizon-Terminal-Bench that preserves its 46 original tasks while correcting task and evaluation-infrastructure defects and extending 31 tasks. items.title: VETNET: Assembling Benchmark Datasets for AI-Driven Veterinary Innovation
items.summary: arXiv:2610.14149v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: VETNET represents an ecosystem of live benchmark datasets and evaluation frameworks designed to accelerate AI-driven innovation in animal science and veterinary medicine through standardized, high-quality datasets and multi-institutional collaboration across academic and non-academic sectors. This framework addresses the gap between AI advances in human medicine and the fragmented state of veterinary AI development.

items.title: Should SLMs be in the Driver's Seat? A Study of Local Models as Interpreters in Cloud-Written Agent Programs
items.summary: arXiv:2610.14209v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The most accurate agents executing user-provided tasks are driven by large, cloud-hosted models, which solve them by reading the private data of the user. items.title: Harness^2: Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World
items.summary: arXiv:2610.14224v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM agents' capabilities depend not only on their underlying models but also on their execution harnesses. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) offers a promising approach to automatically evolve these harnesses. However, deploying RSI in open-world settings still faces two critical challenges. items.summary: arXiv:2610.14277v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tensor parallelism ends every layer with an all-reduce that sits between two dependent matrix multiplications, so its cost cannot be hidden and grows as compute outpaces interconnect bandwidth. items.summary: arXiv:2610.14294v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conditional diffusion models can generate high-quality images that align closely with a given prompt. items.summary: arXiv:2610.14334v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In Model Context Protocol (MCP) systems, LLMs select tools from metadata rather than from their implementations. Names and descriptions summarize what a tool does, while the parameter schema specifies the fields a tool accepts and how they are organized. items.title: Actionable Meta-Requirements for AI Robustness Auditing
items.summary: arXiv:2610.14356v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI-enabled systems must remain dependable when the conditions under which they operate change (e.g., due to input perturbations, distribution shifts, or changes in external dependencies). items.summary: arXiv:2610.14360v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM) alignment often assumes that the user interacting with a model is also the primary beneficiary of its behavior. items.summary: arXiv:2610.14381v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models are increasingly used as scientific assistants, yet we still lack reliable ways to evaluate whether they can investigate a system rather than merely answer a prompt. items.summary: arXiv:2610.14382v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agentic AI systems operating over geospatial data require more than autonomous reasoning and tool use; they must also support explicit orchestration, spatial validation, governance, provenance, failure handling, and human decision authority. items.summary: arXiv:2610.13990v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sparse attention visits few keys, yet finding them can still require scoring every key with every indexer head. items.summary: arXiv:2610.13991v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Self-evolving agents improve through repeated cycles of modification and evaluation. items.summary: arXiv:2610.13995v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Post-training large language models (LLMs) on two-player zero-sum games provides a verifiable reward, and the gains have been shown to transfer to general reasoning. items.summary: arXiv:2610.13998v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proposes a hybrid reinforcement learning trading framework integrating intraday market data with transformer-based financial sentiment signals. items.summary: arXiv:2610.14006v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Since compact, interpretable classifiers correspond to simple programs, it is natural to ask if LLM-based coding agents can be used to learn interpretable models from data. items.title: [Comment] Retatrutide in adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes: what have we learned from TRIUMPH-2?
items.summary: It is a general observation that the degree of weight loss obtained with GLP-1 receptor agonists is less in individuals with type 2 diabetes than in people without diabetes and similar BMI. Could this difference be overcome with the new triple agonists with superior weight-lowering effects? The TRIUMPH-2 study by Virginia Bellido and colleagues1 in The Lancet is a double-blind, parallel-group, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial of the effects of retatrutide, a triple agonist (GLP-1, GIP, and glucagon), in people with obesity and type 2 diabetes.

items.title: [Comment] Offline: Medicine for peace
items.summary: Thomas Hobbes (1588–1679) is most famous for his line in Leviathan (1651) that, “the life of man, solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short”. That proposition may have been true in 17th-century England, but, thanks to the evolution and expansion of health systems, it is not so today for many, although obviously not all. But abstracting that line alone is to miss Hobbes’ wider views about the nature of human being. He believed that without a “common power” ruling over society, our natural tendency is “that condition which is called war…of every man against every man”.

The prevailing assumption appears to be that if a technology can be developed, it should be developed—and that its place in clinical care can be debated afterwards. We believe this sequence should be reversed.

items.title: [Correspondence] The health literacy crisis in the age of AI: lessons from PISA 2025
items.summary: The 2025 Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA) results should concern the health community.1 PISA does not measure health literacy directly, but it assesses several cognitive competencies that increasingly underpin people's ability to navigate health information. For example, in 2025, more than 760 000 students aged 15 years, from 91 countries and economies, participated in the assessment.1 The findings reveal a worrying deterioration in reading, mathematics, and science performance.

items.title: [Correspondence] Taiwan's path to hepatitis C elimination
items.summary: WHO has established a global target to eliminate viral hepatitis as a public health threat by 2030.1 Chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection remains one of the leading causes of cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, and liver-related mortality, affecting an estimated 50 million people worldwide.2 By integrating a comprehensive screening-to-cure cascade, HCV elimination has become an achievable public health goal.

items.title: [Correspondence] Personalising maintenance after tirzepatide weight loss
items.summary: Deborah B Horn and colleagues’ SURMOUNT-MAINTAIN trial provides important evidence that continued tirzepatide is superior to treatment withdrawal for maintaining pharmacologically induced weight loss.1 The trial also shows that reducing tirzepatide to 5 mg offers substantially greater protection against weight regain than switching to placebo. However, the trial's mean effects might not fully convey an important clinical message: response to lower-dose maintenance was heterogeneous.

items.title: [Correspondence] How much can ASTRUM-006 tell us?
items.summary: Lin Shen and colleagues report improved event-free survival with perioperative serplulimab in PD-L1-positive resectable gastric or gastro-oesophageal junction adenocarcinoma.1 The trial is valuable: it selects patients by combined positive score and tests a chemotherapy-free adjuvant phase. However, we urge caution before it is read as practice-changing.

items.title: [Correspondence] Colonoscopy screening and colorectal cancer outcomes: the NordICC trial
items.summary: In their recent Article, Michal F Kaminski and colleagues reported the effects of offering one-time screening colonoscopy at ages 55–64 years after a 13-year follow-up of the NordICC trial.1 Their findings should be interpreted in the context that this trial of a one-time offer of screening colonoscopy was conducted in an era of widespread use of colonoscopy in clinical practice. Estimated reductions in the incidence and mortality of colorectal cancer were much lower than anticipated at trial design.

items.title: [Correspondence] Colonoscopy screening and colorectal cancer outcomes: the NordICC trial
items.summary: The NordICC trial1 should be considered in context with previous colorectal cancer screening studies.2,3 Four randomised controlled trials with more than 458 000 participants show consistent colorectal cancer incidence reductions of 18–23% and larger colorectal cancer mortality reductions of 22–31% with sigmoidoscopy (appendix).3 In the NordICC trial, screening reduced colorectal cancer incidence but not mortality.1

items.title: Wood Street Steps in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania
items.summary: The Wood Street Steps are the last surviving examples of 10 or more stairways Philadelphia founder William Penn commissioned along the original Delaware Riverbank. Why are they important? Penn felt all citizens should have public access to the river wharves. Some early wealthy Quakers, who owned land there, disagreed. As part of a 1684 compromise, Penn made sure at least 10 stairways led to the port area near major cross streets ... from Vine Street to what was originally called Cedar Street ... and is now known as South Street. Unfortunately, this is the only set of those steps left.

items.title: [Articles] Status, challenges, and future directions of machine learning in the management of epilepsy: a systematic review and meta-analysis
items.summary: Although machine learning shows promise in predicting epilepsy treatment outcomes, the high heterogeneity and bias—particularly in small sample sizes, handling of missing data, and scarcity of studies with external validation—limit its clinical applicability. Future research should focus on larger, diverse datasets and standardised minimum reporting. Prospective trials are needed to evaluate machine learning models in real-world settings.

items.title: [Review] Machine learning prediction for epilepsy treatment selection and prognosis: achievements and challenges
items.summary: Accurate prediction of treatment response and selection of optimal treatments remain challenging in epilepsy management. With no reliable surrogate biomarkers for treatment response, the current process of selecting an antiseizure medication remains largely a trial-and-error approach. Other non-pharmacological treatment options, such as epilepsy surgery, are viable alternatives for patients with drug-resistant epilepsy. Statistical and machine learning techniques have been used to predict seizure outcomes associated with antiseizure medications and epilepsy surgery.

items.title: [Review] Artificial intelligence models for automated and semiautomated analysis and interpretation of clinical electroencephalography

Advances in digital technology and wearables have enabled large-scale EEG recording, generating vast amounts of data that cannot be managed through traditional visual interpretation by experts. Artificial intelligence (AI) has the potential to augment human expertise and reduce workloads.
